audit.whatIsWrong: The lane was framed as 'his shadow poke can't match your range'. Razor Shuriken is 900 — exactly Aurora's Q range.
audit.why: 48.11% over 1856 games at 7/10. The early edge is not range, it is conversion and energy: he pays 75 energy per shuriken and needs Shadow Slash at 290 to do real damage, so his walk-up is what you punish. Getting this wrong tells a player to win a poke war they are actually even in.
audit.corrected: early and spikes[0].text now say the ranges match and locate the advantage in his energy costs and 290-range Shadow Slash.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was described as bursting 'from stealth'. Zed has no stealth in his kit.
audit.why: The real spike is Living Shadow (20s at rank 1, 650) stored in brush plus Death Mark's untargetable 625 dash and its 3-second mark. That is a placement threat you answer with vision and with where you stand, not a stealth threat.
audit.corrected: whys[4] and spikes[1].text rebuilt on the shadow-swap plus untargetable dash with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Death Mark is repeatedly described as having a 'reveal' (whys[6], spikes[3].text, late, wants.you[2]). It has no reveal. Riot's text: Zed becomes untargetable, dashes to the target, marks them, and after 3 seconds the mark repeats a portion of the damage he dealt while they were marked. Nothing anywhere mentioned the untargetability.
audit.why: Two consequences were missing. First, burst spent while he is dashing is wasted — the missing-interactions file flags exactly this. Second, the answer to Death Mark is timing, not dodging: you have 3 seconds to not be in range when it triggers, which is what the R teleport and the W hop are for.
audit.corrected: whys[6], spikes[3].text, late, wants.you[2], report[5].t, breakdown.carry and dosFull[0].d now state the untargetable dash and the 3-second mark.

audit.why: Defect item 3. Death Mark 120/110/100, Living Shadow 20/19/18/17/16, Shadow Slash 5s to 3s at 290 range, Razor Shuriken 6s.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the numbers, and with the fact that a spent shadow is a 20-second window.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0..3].side and phases[6].side read 'Skill' while win[0..3] and win[6] read 'Aurora' (matching the packet).
audit.why: Packet, content and the phases whys all describe Aurora owning those rows; the side token was the only dissent.
audit.corrected: Those five sides set to Aurora as one group. Rows 4 and 5 deliberately left untouched — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed in dosFull[1].d (tradeGood verbatim), dontsFull[1].d (wrong body) and dontsFull[2].d (tradeBad verbatim); dosFull[0].d carried the cooldowns sentence; wants.you[3] called his costs 'mana-less' when Zed spends energy.
audit.why: Defect item 2, plus a resource error that removes the only thing you can actually count during his combo.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to their titles; wants.you[3] now names the energy cost.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. It governs your forward steps. - W Across the Veil spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Death Mark: 120s at rank 1, and the mark repeats his damage 3 seconds later — the clock starts when he lands, not when he ults. - Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1, so a spent shadow is a 20s window. - Shadow Slash is 5s and only 290 range.

edits.before: Zed wins by landing Death Mark, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Zed wins by landing Death Mark untargetable, stacking shuriken and Shadow Slash into the 3-second mark, and swapping out.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-recast cleared push that crashes on your trade timers — your patterns farm and poke in the same cast. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with W down — hop-less Aurora is a skinny mage with a haste passive and regrets. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.
edits.after: Best wave: shove it — Zed with a pushed wave either farms under tower or roams, and a roam you ping is a roam that fails. Worst wave: a wave frozen past river with W down, where a shadow in the brush is a free Death Mark. Crash timing: crash, ward, then step back inside your own half of the river.

edits.before: If Zed opens the score, reset expectations and respect Death Mark doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q recasts and stay relevant through zone utility.
edits.after: A fed Zed one-shots inside the 3-second mark, and his passive adds damage to every attack on a low target. Behind, farm at 900, ward the brush he stores shadows in, and never walk past river.

edits.before: Carry through tempo — patterns that exit free compound; your zone turns objective fights into speed checks they fail.
edits.after: Carry by surviving three seconds: Death Mark repeats what he dealt, so break the combo with the hop and he has 120s left.

edits.before: You warp the fight: R the clump, hop through the middle, and pattern whoever the zone slows. The exit portal is your insurance.
edits.after: Late, Zed hunts the flank, not the fight — hold W and R for his 625 dash, drop the zone between you and the shadow, and walk out.

edits.before: Ahead, pace the lane: pattern Zed off every contact, hop his answers, and drop R on each river fight — the zone converts leads into routs.
edits.after: Ahead, shove and deny him energy: he pays 75 per shuriken, so farm him out, ward the brush, and take fights while Death Mark is down.

edits.before: Track Zed’s Death Mark: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Death Mark is 120s: he is untargetable through the dash, so burst spent into it is wasted — answer the mark, which repeats his damage after 3 seconds.

edits.before: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: W is 22s and his Death Mark is 120s — spend the hop after he commits the dash, not on poke, or the 3 seconds kill you.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E the step-up, Q-recast the slowed target, hop out — a full pattern he answered with a whiff.
edits.after: The R zone lets you teleport side to side — fight on its edge so his 625 dash lands you next to your exit.

edits.before: Zed whiffs Death Mark and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: A shoved wave means Zed roams instead of farming — ping it.

edits.before: That is Zed’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: A hop spent on spacing is 22s of no answer to Death Mark.

edits.before: W spent as an entrance is W unavailable as an exit — the whole kit's promise breaks on that one greed.
edits.after: Past river with W down, a shadow in the brush and a 650 swap is all he needs to start the three seconds.

edits.before: Hopping IN with W and trading while his engage is still loaded — the exit spent as an entrance is how Auroras get coached postmortem.
edits.after: His passive adds bonus damage to attacks on low targets, so at half HP the recast you stayed for is the reason the mark finishes you.

edits.before: Zed's Death Mark grants a real burst-engage window from stealth that can kill Aurora before her escape is ready.
edits.after: Death Mark makes Zed untargetable as he dashes 625 onto you, and the mark repeats his damage 3 seconds later.

edits.before: Item power plus R's dodge for Death Mark's reveal make Aurora safe and dominant in extended play.
edits.after: Item power plus the R teleport lets Aurora walk out of range before the 3-second mark detonates.

edits.before: Zed's Shadow poke is weak into your Q Twin Drift range, and your E Weirding punishes any Q3 shuriken-return dash he tries before he has Ult, so he's stuck farming under tower most of levels 3-5.
edits.after: Razor Shuriken matches your 900 range but costs him 75 energy a cast, and Shadow Slash needs 290 — so he pays for every poke while your E punishes the walk-up, and before 6 he has no way to finish you.

edits.before: Zed's Death Mark spike is real and sudden — he can shadow-swap in from fog or a bush and burst you before your R Between Worlds is ready to bail, so this is genuinely his window, not yours.
edits.after: Death Mark is his window: he drops Living Shadow in brush, swaps 650 to it, then ults untargetable from 625 — the burst is all front-loaded into three seconds you cannot outrun standing still.

edits.before: By 2+ items your R Between Worlds gives you a clean dodge for his Death Mark reveal-burst combo, and your ranged zone denies him the Shadow-dash approach entirely — he's forced to wait for picks elsewhere.
edits.after: By 2+ items Between Worlds' teleport gets you out of the three seconds Death Mark gives him, and the E slow catches him the moment he swaps back to Living Shadow — he has to look for picks elsewhere.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 you're clearly ahead — Zed's shadow-based poke can't match Q Twin Drift at range, and any shadow-dash approach walks straight into your E slow, so he's forced into a passive farming pattern that costs him tempo and sets up nothing.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 you're ahead on trades, not on range — Razor Shuriken also reaches 900, but it costs 75 energy and he has no way to convert the chip, while any walk-up for Shadow Slash at 290 hands you a free E slow and a Q recast.

edits.before: Once your first item lands you're back in firm control, and by 2+ items your R Between Worlds is a clean answer to his ult reveal-burst — hold it specifically for that combo rather than for damage, and your ranged zone keeps him from ever finding a safe all-in angle again.
edits.after: Once your first item lands you're back in firm control, and by 2+ items Between Worlds answers Death Mark directly — the mark repeats his damage after 3 seconds, so hold the R to be somewhere else when it lands, and keep the E for the shadow he swaps to.

edits.before: Poke with Q Twin Drift and back off before his shadow range
edits.after: Poke with Q at 900 and step back before Living Shadow lands

edits.before: Save R Between Worlds to slip out of his Death Mark reveal, not for extra damage
edits.after: Save R Between Worlds to be out of range when the 3-second mark finally triggers

edits.before: Punish his mana-less all-ins with E's slow after he shadow-dashes in
edits.after: Punish the energy cost of his combo with E's slow as he lands on you

notes: 1) The packet's suspect name 'Death Mark's' is a FALSE POSITIVE on the name — but the sentence around it was wrong for a different reason: Death Mark has no reveal. That fabricated 'reveal' appears in four separate fields here (whys[6], spikes[3].text, late, wants.you[2]), so it is worth grepping the repo for 'reveal' near 'Death Mark' on other champions. 2) DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE — rows 4 and 5 of the chart. The prose everywhere (whys[4], spikes[1] 'Lvl 6', spikes[2] '1st item', mid) says level 6 is Zed's window and first item is Aurora's. The packet levelChart and win[] say the opposite: win[4]=Aurora, win[5]=Zed. The chart may be shifted one row, or the packet may be treating 6+Youmuu's as the real spike. Per the chart rule I did not move a row I could not settle from the kit, and I did not touch phases[4].side (currently 'Zed', disagreeing with win[4]) or phases[5].side. This needs a human decision — see questionsForUser. 3) 'Q Twin Drift' and 'E Weirding' recur here; I removed 'Twin Drift' from the fields I edited since the brief carries no Aurora ability names to verify against. 4) Zed spends energy, not mana — wants.you[3] said 'mana-less all-ins', which loses the only resource you can count during his combo.
